summary: James Burnes worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1817 to 1820 and earned an LL.D. at the University of Glasgow in 1834.

James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who earned his PhD from Yale University in 1984. Attested between 2015 and 2019, he served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College.

James C. Harle worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning degrees from Princeton (B.A.) and Oxford (B.A., D.Phil., D.Litt.). He was an Assistant to the Dean at Princeton (1947–1949) and Assistant Keeper (1960) and Keeper (1967–1987) at the Ashmolean Museum.

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College, Fort William College, and under Thomas Roebuck. He served as Registrar at Calcutta High Court (1810), Principal of Hooghly Mohsin College (1839), and professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Lycée Condorcet and EPHE under Bréal, Bergaigne, and Hauvette-Besnault. He taught at EPHE (directorship in 1892) and was Professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Drummond Anderson worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Cheltenham College, Rugby School, and Cambridge (M.A. circa 1907–1909), served in the Indian Civil Service (1875–1900), and became University Lecturer in Bengali at Cambridge in 1907.

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under Sheldon Pollock, later becoming Professor Emeritus at the University of Iowa, where his post began in 1971.
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College from circa 1830 to 1833. He later held a post at Yale University from circa 1850 to 1892.

James Fairbrother Edwards specialized in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Handsworth Theological College around 1904 to 1907 and served as Principal of the United Theological College, Pune, in 1930.

James Fergusson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at the Royal High School. He became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840 and served as secretary to A. H. Layard at the Office of Works in 1868.

James Fieser is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Berea College and Purdue University. He held posts at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, and at the University of Tennessee at Martin around 1992.

James Fuller Blumhardt worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge (1883–1888), in the British Museum's Oriental manuscripts department (circa 1886–1922), and as Lecturer in Bengali at University College London (circa 1896–1922).

James G. Mullens specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Simon Fraser, Victoria, and McMaster (PhD 1994) under Graeme MacQueen, Yün-hua Jan, and John G. Arapura, and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Grant Liston Garthwaite worked in linguistics and Indology and earned a B.A. from Westminster College, London. He served as a missionary and teacher with the Basel Mission (circa 1857–1869) and was a Fellow at the University of Madras in 1884.

James Grant Stephen specialized in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge, where he studied from circa 1857 to 1861, and served there as Lecturer in Hindustani from 1860 to 1863.

James Gray was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Akyab Government High School (1872), served as Professor of Pāli at Basic Education High School No. 1 Dagon, and was Professor of Pali at the University of Rangoon (circa 1884–1905).

James H. Austin, a scholar in neurology and Buddhist studies, trained under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at Oregon Health & Science University (circa 1960–1967) and the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (circa 1967–1992).

James Hadley worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Fairfield Academy, Yale (B.A. 1844), and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury. He served as a tutor at Middlebury College (1845) and was an assistant professor at Yale University from 1845 to 1872.

James Hair Maclean worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow (M.A. circa 1886–1890), Oxford, and Jena, and served as a missionary for the United Free Church of Scotland in 1895.

James Haughton Woods was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Harvard, Episcopal Divinity School, Berlin, Oxford, and Strasbourg (Ph.D. 1897), studying under Deussen, Venis, and Lanman. He served at Harvard as Assistant in History (1891) and Professor (1913–1934).
